source.anchor_kjv: All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee.
source.thread: The psalm of one forsaken man dying alone ends with all the ends of the world turning to the LORD - the reach of the cross
source.hook_line: Psalm twenty-two opens with one forsaken man dying alone and ends with every nation on earth.
source.spoken_script: Psalm twenty-two opens with one forsaken man dying alone and ends with every nation on earth. After the suffering, the song throws its arms open to every nation: "All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee." A man dying in one corner of the Roman Empire and his song says the ends of the earth will turn to God. It sounded impossible. But from that cross, and the empty tomb, the gospel went out and people in nation after nation have turned to the LORD, worshipping the One who died and rose. That is the reach of the cross. It was never a local tragedy it was for the nations, all the kindreds of the earth. And "the ends of the world" includes wherever you are, right now. The song that began with one man dying alone has swept the whole earth; the Lord it promised still has room for you to turn to Him.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- tiktok (precision): "nation after nation has turned to the LORD" quietly upgrades the video's claim. The narration says "people in nation after nation have turned" - people within nations, not nations as converted units. Fix: "people in nation after nation have turned to the LORD."
- instagram (attribution, minor): the caption opens with a verbatim KJV fragment ("all the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD") with no quote marks. The next sentence does name Psalm 22, so it is not orphaned, but adding "Psalm 22:" before the line would make the quotation honest at a glance. Non-blocking.
- Cross-sibling consistency check (non-blocking, verified): this kit says the psalm "ends with every nation" (v27) while the sibling he_hath_done_this kit calls v31 the psalm's "last line." No contradiction: vv27-31 form the psalm's closing movement about the nations, and v31 is its final line; both kits mirror their own video's hook. Leave as is.
- KJV check: Psalm 22:27 verbatim, correctly attributed, front-loaded in YT/FB. PASS.
- Titles: chosen title is the video's own arc, honest, no sibling collision. Facebook title is a verbatim line from the narration. PASS.
- Grace check: "still has room for you to turn to him" is the video's own landing; invitation, no fear framing. PASS.
